zoe_cs: Drafting a tiny 'launchpad' cheat-sheet for the startup trial kickoff tomorrow. Needs to be single page, customer-facing, and cover cache / batch / stream + quick verification.

zoe_cs: LAUNCHPAD CHEAT-SHEET (one page) TL;DR: cache-first for repeated prompts; batch for many small concurrent calls; stream for interactive apps. Have a simple rollback.

zoe_cs: PRE-LAUNCH CHECKS
- Warm pool >= expected TPS for first 90m (recommend 1.2x if unsure).
- Telemetry wired: p95 latency, 5xx rate, cache-hit-rate, batch-size histograms. Owner: platform-observability.

zoe_cs: CACHE (simple rules)
- Use prefix cache for repeated heads (>25% identical starts).
- Suggested TTLs: session prompts 5-15m, static/system prompts 12-24h.
- Use stale-while-revalidate for UX.
- Quick test (curl):
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hello","cache_key":"lp_greet_v1"}' -i
# repeat -> expect header x-cache: HIT
```

zoe_cs: BATCHING (practical knobs)
- For many small requests (<150 tokens) enable batching. Start window 10ms, max 75ms. MaxBatch: 64 on heavy GPUs, 32 on small.
- Recommend a short probe during business hours (200 concurrent small requests labelled probe=true) so we can tune.

li_eng: Add sample SDK config (pseudocode):
```js
client.configureBatching({ initialWindowMs:10, maxWindowMs:75, maxBatchSize:64 });
```

zoe_cs: STREAMING
- Streaming for chat/live assistants. Flush partial tokens every 40-80ms or on sentence boundary.
- If stream drops, retry once after 200ms then fall back to non-stream endpoint.

ram_sre: Ops notes: for Dedicated, cap per-tenant cache entries (e.g., max_entries=5000) to avoid noisy neighbours. Enable soft eviction on OOM. Trace sampling 10% for first 48h, then 1%.

zoe_cs: ROLLBACK TRIGGERS (customer-facing)
- If p95 latency >2x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes: set cache TTL=0 and reduce batch window to 5ms; notify ops.
- Circuit breaker suggestion: open if 5xx > 3% over 60s, cool down 30s.

zoe_cs: QUICK VERIFICATION (5 min)
1) Run perf script -> record baseline tokens/s and p95 latency.
2) Cache smoke -> perform curl above x3 -> expect HIT on 2nd request.
3) Batch probe -> run small probe during business hours and share observed batch sizes.
4) Stream smoke -> open stream, send 3 prompts, confirm partial flush within 100ms.

li_eng: I'll add the perf script link and a short rollback playbook snippet.
